Prol. Dies ist die Satzung, die der König der Engländer und sowohl geweihte wie Laien-Witan erkoren und bestimmt haben.
Prologue. This is the ordinance which the king of the English and both the ecclesiastical and lay witan have chosen and decided.
This is the ordinance which has been determined upon and enacted by the king of England and his councillors, both ecclesiastic and lay.
This is the ordinance which the king of the English and both ecclesiastical and lay councillors have approved and decreed.
This is the decree which the king of the English and both his ecclesiastical and secular councilors have approved and proclaimed.

This is the first datable code drafted in the style of Archbishop Wulfstan. It surivives in C.C.C.C., MS. 201, which contains many of his works, and twice in that part of B.L.Cott. Nero A. 1 which has entries in his own hand. A very similar code, cited as VI Ethelred, survives both in English and in Latin in another manuscript, B.L.Cott. Claud.A. iii, which has entries in Wulfstan’s hand. The Latin version says it was promulgated at Enham, and expressly states that Wulfstan had taken part in its drafting. The English version is in his style. There are differences between V and VI Ethelred, and the best explanation of them is that given by Dr Sisam, namely that after a council at Enham in 1008 Wulfstan was empowered to produce a modified version for the northern part of the country, and that the Latin version was drawn up by him for circulation among the higher ecclesiastics, while the English version of VI, for general circulation, was made by working over V Ethelred in relation to the Latin version. My text is translated from the first of the two texts in Nero A. 1, which has the Latin rubric: “In the name of the Lord, in the year of our Lord’s incarnation 1008”. The second version in Nero has merely, in English, “Concerning the ordinance of the councillors”. C.C.C.C. 201 has a Latin rubric, “In the name of the Lord.” The Latin of VI Ethelred is headed: “Incipiunt sinodalia decreta” and the English: “Concerning the ordinance of the councillors”. V Ethelred is edited by Liebermann, I, 236–47; and with translation by Robertson, pp. 78–91, by Thorpe, I, 304–13. In all three editions the English of VI Ethelred follows, but the Latin version is only in Liebermann, I, 247–57. [Her footnote 1: Studies in the History of Old English Literature, pp. 278–87]
